title: Open wide subgroupoids induce representable etale quotient-stack maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. For a groupoid in schemes, use the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]; for algebraic spaces use the same laws on all test-scheme points. Write $[V/R]$ for the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $V(T)$-objects and $R(T)$-arrows [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Let $(V,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$ with $s,t$ flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $P\subseteq R$ be an open subspace containing the unit and stable under inverse and composition, with all the same objects $V$; an open subspace means a subfunctor whose scheme base changes are open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $[V/P]$ and $[V/R]$ are algebraic stacks, and inclusion induces a morphism $j:[V/P]\to[V/R]$ which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Algebraic stack means a stack with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Surjectivity means field-extension-local lifting of field-valued objects. If $[V/R]$ is Deligne--Mumford, then $[V/P]$ is Deligne--Mumford as well.

source.place: Tag 0DU2 (lemma-quasi-splitting-etale), complete statement. The final DM consequence follows by pulling back an etale scheme atlas and taking etale scheme charts of its algebraic-space pullbacks; equivalently Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal Y=[V/P]$ and $\mathcal X=[V/R]$. On scheme charts an open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; the chartwise calculus [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] makes it flat and locally of finite presentation and preserves these properties under composition. Thus $s|_P,t|_P$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] to $(V,R)$ and $(V,P)$. Both quotients are algebraic stacks; their object maps are representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. The inclusion of test-point groupoids extends to $j:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ by the universal extension property of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description].

For $a,b\in\mathcal Y(T)$ choose a common fppf covering on which both come from $V$-objects; this is permitted by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Between such objects their Isom sheaves are the corresponding fibres of $P$ and $R$: these are already sheaves, since algebraic spaces are fppf sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The map is injective since $P$ is an open subfunctor of $R$. Hence two arrows $a\to b$ with the same image under $j$ agree on the cover and agree globally, since Isom presheaves of a stack are sheaves. Thus $j$ is faithful on every fibre. Now [lem-sfb-faithful-stack-map-representable] implies that $j$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 0DU2, first paragraph: monicity and fibrewise faithfulness; algebraic.tex Tag 04Y5.

proof.text: Given a field-valued object $x$ of $\mathcal X$, surjectivity of $V\to\mathcal X$ in [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] gives a field extension and $v\in V$ representing $x$ after that extension. The same $v$ defines an object of $\mathcal Y$, whose image under $j$ is the chosen representative of $x$. This proves the asserted field-extension-local surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0DU2, first paragraph: field-valued objects and surjectivity.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-quotient-map-cartesian-action-groupoid] to $(V,P)\to(V,R)$. It identifies $V\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y$ with $[R/B]$, where $B=P\times_{s,V,t}R$, source is $(p,r)\mapsto r$, target is $(p,r)\mapsto c(p,r)$, and the map to $V$ is induced by $s:R\to V$. This is a groupoid over $V$ since $s(c(p,r))=s(r)$. Its relation map to $R\times_{s,V,s}R$ is an open immersion: the mutually inverse formulas
$$(p,r)\longmapsto(c(p,r),r),\qquad(r_1,r_2)\longmapsto(c(r_1,i(r_2)),r_2)$$
identify $B$ with the inverse image of the open subspace $P\subset R$ under $(r_1,r_2)\mapsto c(r_1,i(r_2))$. The groupoid laws [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], interpreted on test schemes as in the statement, verify the formulas: $c(c(p,r),i(r))=p$ and $c(c(r_1,i(r_2)),r_2)=r_1$. Pullback of an open subfunctor is open, since on a scheme it is inverse image of an open subscheme. Because $s:R\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, [lem-sfb-open-relation-etale-quotient] applies over $Y=V$. Hence $V\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y\to V$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 0DU2, second paragraph: 04Y4 action presentation and application of 0DU1.

proof.text: The cover $V\to\mathcal X$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient]. Step 2 proved representability of $j$, so the target-local etaleness assertion of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] applies to this cover. Step 4 proves its base-change test. Thus $j$ is etale.

Assume $\mathcal X$ is Deligne--Mumford. Choose its surjective etale scheme atlas $A\to\mathcal X$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representability of $j$ gives the algebraic space $B=A\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Y$. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $C\to B$, available by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $B\to\mathcal Y$ is surjective etale (base change of $A\to\mathcal X$), and its composition with $C\to B$ is surjective etale and representable. Thus $C\to\mathcal Y$ is an etale scheme atlas. The diagonal of $\mathcal Y$ is already representable by step 1, so this is precisely the Deligne--Mumford definition.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), atlas criterion, and the definition of a Deligne--Mumford stack.

lean.statement: theorem open_subgroupoid_etale_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {V R P : AlgebraicSpace S} (s t : R ⟶ V) (e : V.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (i : R.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (c : Limits.pullback s.hom.hom t.hom.hom ⟶ R.obj.obj) (q : P.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (hq : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left) q) (eP : V.obj.obj ⟶ P.obj.obj) (iP : P.obj.obj ⟶ P.obj.obj) (cP : Limits.pullback (q ≫ s.hom.hom) (q ≫ t.hom.hom) ⟶ P.obj.obj) (he : eP ≫ q = e) (hi : iP ≫ q = q ≫ i) (hc : cP ≫ q = pullback.map (q ≫ s.hom.hom) (q ≫ t.hom.hom) s.hom.hom t.hom.hom q q (𝟙 V.obj.obj) (by simp) (by simp) ≫ c) (hs : MapIsFlat s) (ht : MapIsFlat t) (hsfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation s) (htfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation t) (X : BasedCategory.{max u v₁, max (u + 1) w₁} (Over S)) (Y : BasedCategory.{max u v₂, max (u + 1) w₂} (Over S)) (aR : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli V.obj.obj) X) (aP : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli V.obj.obj) Y) (hR : SpaceGroupoidQuotientPresentation s.hom.hom t.hom.hom e i c X aR) (hP : SpaceGroupoidQuotientPresentation (q ≫ s.hom.hom) (q ≫ t.hom.hom) eP iP cP Y aP) : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Y ∧ IsAlgebraicModuliStack X ∧ ∃ (j : BasedFunctor Y X) (β : ModuliTwoIso (aP.comp j) aR), (∀ z : (discreteModuli P.obj.obj).obj, j.map (hP.arrows.val.hom.app z) ≫ β.val.hom.app ((discreteModuliMap (q ≫ t.hom.hom)).obj z) = β.val.hom.app ((discreteModuliMap (q ≫ s.hom.hom)).obj z) ≫ hR.arrows.val.hom.app ((discreteModuliMap q).obj z)) ∧ IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces j ∧ IsSurjectiveModuliMap j ∧ ModuliSpaceTest (@Etale) j ∧ (IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack X → IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack Y)
